content.user_title: Build and Optimize React Three Fiber Scenes
content.value_statement: React Three Fiber scenes can waste CPU and GPU resources through inefficient animation, loading, and rendering. This skill guides implementation choices for frame loops, instancing, assets, and adaptive quality.
actual_capabilities: Guide Canvas setup, pixel ratio limits, demand rendering, and frame invalidation.
Explain delta-based mesh animation and reusable allocations without per-frame React state updates.
Recommend shared geometries, materials, and instancing to reduce rendering overhead.
Guide cached model loading, preloading, compression, and progressive loading with Suspense.
Recommend level of detail, adaptive quality, lighting, shadows, and postprocessing tradeoffs.
Explain resource cleanup and profiling through frame statistics, draw calls, and triangle counts.
limitations: Provides guidance and short examples, not a complete application or automated optimization tool.
Targets React Three Fiber and drei rather than every Three.js or general 3D workflow.
Does not include models, textures, compression tools, or benchmark results.
API compatibility and performance depend on installed versions and target devices.

use_cases.title: Create a Product Viewer
use_cases.description: Configure demand rendering, cached model loading, and progressive loading for a product viewer that becomes idle.

use_cases.title: Optimize Repeated Scene Objects
use_cases.description: Compare shared resources, drei instancing, and raw InstancedMesh updates for scenes with many repeated objects.

use_cases.title: Review Rendering Bottlenecks
use_cases.description: Inspect frame-loop allocations, draw calls, lighting, and adaptive quality choices before selecting performance changes.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up a Basic Viewer
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me configure a React Three Fiber product viewer using drei. Recommend Canvas settings and explain when demand rendering needs invalidation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: configuring a scene that becomes idle.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Mesh Animation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React Three Fiber animation: [component]. Replace per-frame state updates and repeated allocations with delta-based mutation and reusable objects.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Asset Loading
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my React Three Fiber model-loading flow: [details]. Recommend caching, preloading, compression, and Suspense boundaries compatible with my installed versions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: managing large models and textures.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Scene Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this React Three Fiber scene: [scene and measurements]. Compare instancing, raw InstancedMesh, adaptive quality, lighting changes, and cleanup.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: selecting optimizations from measured bottlenecks.

output_examples.input: Review a React Three Fiber viewer that keeps rendering while idle.
output: Recommend demand rendering for the idle viewer.
Identify imperative changes that require frame invalidation.
Keep rendering active during animation and measure behavior on target devices.

output_examples.input: Review a scene with many repeated meshes and high draw-call counts.
output: Recommend sharing geometry and materials across repeated meshes.
Compare drei Instances with raw InstancedMesh for the expected object count.
Measure draw calls and CPU overhead before accepting the optimization.

output_examples.input: Review inconsistent motion and repeated allocations in an animation loop.
output: Move reusable temporary objects outside the frame loop.
Avoid routing continuous animation through React state updates.

best_practices: Profile React work, draw calls, allocations, and GPU costs before selecting an optimization.
Check React, React Three Fiber, drei, and Three.js versions and peer dependencies together.
Choose the frame loop deliberately and dispose resources created imperatively.
anti_patterns: Updating React state or allocating temporary objects on every animation frame.
Using demand rendering without invalidation for imperative changes or ongoing animation.
Applying universal draw-call limits or quality settings without measuring target devices.

faq.question: What does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It guides React Three Fiber and drei scene setup, animation, loading, instancing, adaptive quality, profiling, and cleanup.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does the skill run benchmarks automatically?
faq.answer: No. It recommends profiling methods and metrics, but includes no benchmark scripts or automated measurements.

faq.question: When should I use demand rendering?
faq.answer: Use it for scenes that become idle. Imperative mutations require invalidation, and ongoing animation needs repeated invalidation or a continuous loop.

faq.question: Does instancing always solve performance problems?
faq.answer: No. Instancing can reduce draw calls, but React-backed instances still incur CPU costs. Measure alternatives for large populations.

faq.question: Can I use this skill for any Three.js project?
faq.answer: Its focus is React Three Fiber and drei. It is not intended for every plain Three.js or general 3D task.
